This page describes the numerical algorithms used in hftest, covering: Boys function evaluation, the McMurchie-Davidson integral engine, direct SCF with Schwarz screening, and Pulay DIIS.

Boys Function

The Boys function of order \(n\) appears as the fundamental building block of all nuclear-attraction and electron-repulsion integrals over Gaussian basis functions:

(1)\[F_n(x) = \int_0^1 t^{2n}\, e^{-x t^2}\, dt = \frac{1}{2}\, x^{-(n+\tfrac{1}{2})}\, \gamma\!\left(n+\tfrac{1}{2},\, x\right),\]

where \(\gamma\) is the lower incomplete Gamma function.

Regime 1 — Trivial limit (\(x \le 10^{-14}\))

When \(x \approx 0\) the integrand equals \(t^{2n}\) and

\[F_n(0) = \frac{1}{2n+1}.\]

Regime 2 — Taylor series (\(0 < x < 1\))

For small positive \(x\) the exponential is expanded:

\[F_n(x) = \int_0^1 t^{2n}\sum_{k=0}^\infty \frac{(-x)^k t^{2k}}{k!}\,dt = \sum_{k=0}^\infty \frac{(-x)^k}{k!\,(2n+2k+1)}.\]

The partial-sum loop breaks when the absolute term drops below \(10^{-16}\) (typically converges in fewer than 30 terms for \(x < 1\)).

Regime 3 — Analytic \(F_0\) + upward recurrence (\(x \ge 1\))

For large \(x\) the \(n = 0\) case has the closed form

\[F_0(x) = \frac{\sqrt{\pi}}{2\sqrt{x}}\,\operatorname{erf}(\sqrt{x}).\]

Higher orders are then generated by the upward recurrence:

(2)\[F_{n+1}(x) = \frac{(2n+1)\,F_n(x) - e^{-x}}{2x}.\]

For very large \(x\), cancellation in (2) can make the result non-finite. In that case the asymptotic approximation is used as a fallback:

\[F_n(x) \approx \frac{(2n-1)!!\,\sqrt{\pi}}{2^{n+1}\, x^{n+\tfrac{1}{2}}} \quad (x \to \infty).\]

The function boys_Fvec(nmax, x, F[]) computes all orders \(F_0, F_1, \ldots, F_{n_\text{max}}\) in a single pass, which is critical for performance in the integral engine.

McMurchie-Davidson Integral Engine

All one- and two-electron integrals are computed using the McMurchie-Davidson (MD) scheme [MD1978]. The key idea is to expand a product of two Cartesian Gaussians

\[G_{ij}(r,\alpha,\beta,X_{AB}) = (r-A)^i\,e^{-\alpha(r-A)^2}\cdot(r-B)^j\,e^{-\beta(r-B)^2}\]

as a linear combination of Hermite Gaussians centred at \(P = (\alpha A+\beta B)/p\):

\[G_{ij} = \sum_{t=0}^{i+j} E_t^{ij}(\alpha,\beta,X_{AB})\, \Lambda_t(p, r-P),\qquad \Lambda_t(p,x) = \left(-\frac{\partial}{\partial P}\right)^t e^{-p(r-P)^2}.\]

E-Coefficients

The expansion coefficients \(E_t^{ij}\) satisfy the three-term recursion (one Cartesian direction at a time):

\[\begin{split}E_t^{i+1,j} &= \frac{1}{2p} E_{t-1}^{ij} + X_{PA}\, E_t^{ij} + (t+1)\, E_{t+1}^{ij} \\[4pt] E_t^{i,j+1} &= \frac{1}{2p} E_{t-1}^{ij} + X_{PB}\, E_t^{ij} + (t+1)\, E_{t+1}^{ij}\end{split}\]

starting from \(E_0^{00} = e^{-\mu X_{AB}^2}\) with \(\mu = \alpha\beta/p\).

The implementation stores the full table E[i][j][t] with \(i,j \le 8\) and \(t \le i+j\) as a stack array of size [9][9][18] (ETable).

R-Integrals

The auxiliary Hermite integrals required for nuclear-attraction (NA) and ERI evaluation are:

\[R_{tuv}^n = (-2p)^n\, \frac{\partial^t}{\partial P_x^t} \frac{\partial^u}{\partial P_y^u} \frac{\partial^v}{\partial P_z^v} \frac{1}{r}\bigg|_{r=|\mathbf{P}-\mathbf{C}|}\]

with base case

\[R_{000}^n = F_n(p\,R_{PC}^2)\]

and recursion [HJO2000b] (eq. 9.9.18):

\[\begin{split}R_{t+1,u,v}^n &= t\,R_{t-1,u,v}^{n+1} + X_{PC}\,R_{tuv}^{n+1} \\ R_{t,u+1,v}^n &= u\,R_{t,u-1,v}^{n+1} + Y_{PC}\,R_{tuv}^{n+1} \\ R_{t,u,v+1}^n &= v\,R_{t,u,v-1}^{n+1} + Z_{PC}\,R_{tuv}^{n+1}.\end{split}\]

The table R[n][t][u][v] is stored as [20][20][20][20] doubles on the thread-local stack.

One-Electron Integrals

Overlap \(S_{\mu\nu} = \langle\mu|\nu\rangle\)

For primitives \((\mathbf{a}, \ell_a)\) and \((\mathbf{b}, \ell_b)\):

\[S_{\mu\nu} = E_0^{n_{x,a}\,n_{x,b}}\,E_0^{n_{y,a}\,n_{y,b}}\,E_0^{n_{z,a}\,n_{z,b}} \cdot \left(\frac{\pi}{p}\right)^{3/2}.\]

Kinetic energy \(T_{\mu\nu} = \langle\mu|-\tfrac{1}{2}\nabla^2|\nu\rangle\)

Using the Obara-Saika relation [OS1986]:

\[T_{\mu\nu} = \beta(2\ell_b+3)\,S_{\mu\nu}^{(b)} - 2\beta^2\,S_{\mu\nu}^{(b+2)} - \tfrac{1}{2}\ell_b(\ell_b-1)\,S_{\mu\nu}^{(b-2)}\]

where \(S^{(b\pm 2)}\) denotes the overlap integral with the angular momentum of centre B raised/lowered by one unit (total) in the relevant Cartesian direction, expressed via E-coefficient tables accumulated at the same \(p\).

Nuclear attraction \(V_{\mu\nu} = \langle\mu|{-Z_A}/{r_{1A}}|\nu\rangle\)

\[V_{\mu\nu} = \frac{2\pi}{p} \sum_A (-Z_A) \sum_{tuv} E_t^{(x)}\,E_u^{(y)}\,E_v^{(z)}\, R_{tuv}^0\]

summed over all nuclear centres \(A\).

Two-Electron Integrals (ERIs)

The four-centre ERI

\[(\mu\nu|\lambda\sigma) = \iint \chi_\mu(\mathbf{r}_1)\chi_\nu(\mathbf{r}_1)\,\frac{1}{r_{12}}\, \chi_\lambda(\mathbf{r}_2)\chi_\sigma(\mathbf{r}_2)\, d\mathbf{r}_1\,d\mathbf{r}_2\]

factorises (after Gaussian product theorem applied to both pairs) as

\[(\mu\nu|\lambda\sigma) = \frac{2\pi^{5/2}}{p\,q\sqrt{p+q}} \sum_{t_1 u_1 v_1} \sum_{t_2 u_2 v_2} E_{t_1}^{(x,12)}\,E_{u_1}^{(y,12)}\,E_{v_1}^{(z,12)}\, E_{t_2}^{(x,34)}\,E_{u_2}^{(y,34)}\,E_{v_2}^{(z,34)}\, (-1)^{t_2+u_2+v_2}\, R_{t_1+t_2,u_1+u_2,v_1+v_2}^0\]

where \(p = \alpha_1+\alpha_2\), \(q = \alpha_3+\alpha_4\), \(\mathbf{W} = (p\mathbf{P}+q\mathbf{Q})/(p+q)\), and the R-integrals are evaluated at \(\mathbf{W}-\mathbf{P}\) with parameter \(\rho = pq/(p+q)\).

The Boys vector is computed once per primitive quartet with boys_Fvec(nmax, rho*RPQ², F) where \(n_\text{max}\) is the sum of all four angular momenta.

Shell Normalization

After primitive contractions are assembled, each shell is normalized so that its diagonal overlap matrix element equals 1:

\[N_\mu = \frac{1}{\sqrt{\langle\mu|\mu\rangle}}.\]

This is applied to all contracted functions within the shell simultaneously, matching the convention used by Gaussian09 and Psi4.

Direct SCF and Schwarz Screening

Direct SCF recomputes all ERIs every iteration — no disk storage. This scales as \(\mathcal{O}(N_b^4)\) naively but is accelerated by the Schwarz inequality: for a shell quartet \((\mu\nu|\lambda\sigma)\)

\[|(\mu\nu|\lambda\sigma)| \le \sqrt{(\mu\nu|\mu\nu)}\,\sqrt{(\lambda\sigma|\lambda\sigma)}.\]

Define the Schwarz matrix \(Q_{\mu\nu} = \sqrt{(\mu\nu|\mu\nu)}\). Shell quartets are skipped entirely when

\[Q_{\mu\nu}^{\rm shell}\cdot Q_{\lambda\sigma}^{\rm shell} < \varepsilon_{\rm screen}\]

(default \(\varepsilon_{\rm screen} = 10^{-10}\)). Within a surviving shell quartet, individual basis-function pairs are also screened before accumulating into \(\mathbf{J}\) and \(\mathbf{K}\).

The J/K build exploits the 8-fold permutational symmetry of real ERIs:

\[(\mu\nu|\lambda\sigma) = (\nu\mu|\lambda\sigma) = (\mu\nu|\sigma\lambda) = (\lambda\sigma|\mu\nu) = \ldots\]

so each unique quartet is computed once.

Pulay DIIS Convergence Acceleration

Without acceleration, the SCF iteration

\[P_{\rm new} = \text{diagonalize}\bigl(F[P]\bigr)\]

may converge only linearly or oscillate. Direct Inversion in the Iterative Subspace (DIIS) [Pulay1980] constructs a better Fock matrix as a linear combination of previous iterates:

\[\mathbf{F}_\text{DIIS} = \sum_{i=1}^m c_i\, \mathbf{F}_i\]

where the coefficients \(c_i\) minimise the error norm subject to \(\sum_i c_i = 1\).

Error Vector

The DIIS error vector is taken as the commutator of the Fock and density matrices in the orthogonal AO basis:

\[\mathbf{e} = \mathbf{F}\mathbf{P}\mathbf{S} - \mathbf{S}\mathbf{P}\mathbf{F}.\]

When \(\mathbf{e} = 0\) the density matrix satisfies the idempotency and the Fock equations simultaneously, so this is a well- motivated measure of SCF error.

DIIS Linear System

The DIIS equations form the bordered linear system

\[\begin{split}\begin{pmatrix} B_{11} & \cdots & B_{1m} & -1 \\ \vdots & \ddots & \vdots & \vdots \\ B_{m1} & \cdots & B_{mm} & -1 \\ -1 & \cdots & -1 & 0 \end{pmatrix} \begin{pmatrix} c_1 \\ \vdots \\ c_m \\ \lambda \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 0 \\ \vdots \\ 0 \\ -1 \end{pmatrix}\end{split}\]

where \(B_{ij} = \langle \mathbf{e}_i | \mathbf{e}_j \rangle = \operatorname{Tr}(\mathbf{e}_i^\top \mathbf{e}_j)\).

This is solved via at::linalg_solve. If the matrix is singular (a degenerate subspace), the program falls back to the most recent Fock matrix.

SCF Convergence Criterion

Convergence is declared when both of the following are satisfied simultaneously:

\[|\Delta E| < \varepsilon \quad \text{and} \quad \text{RMS}(\Delta \mathbf{P}) < \varepsilon\]

where \(\varepsilon\) is the user-supplied convergence threshold (default \(10^{-8}\)).

The initial guess for the density matrix is obtained from the core-Hamiltonian (bare-nucleus) Fock matrix: diagonalise \(\mathbf{H}^{\rm core}\) in the orthogonal basis, occupy the \(N/2\) lowest orbitals, and form \(\mathbf{P}^{(0)}\).
